items.title: France to impose new curfews where necessary: PM
items.description:
France will impose new curfews in areas where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the measures introduced in several cities the previous day had “helped keep the night calm”.
France was rocked on Saturday by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before the country elects a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.
Accused of failing to anticipate and contain the street violence, the government has pledged to restore order, and had announced partial curfews in Paris and some other cities on Monday.

items.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada
items.description:
Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province’s first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the US.
CBC News, Canada’s government-funded national broadcaster, called the result late Monday after 33 per cent of the vote had been counted. At the time of the call, 76pc of tallied votes were in support of the “remain” side versus 23pc in favour of the province moving forward with a binding vote on separation. The referendum was nonbinding.

items.title: Declared dead: Indian voters fight to get back on electoral rolls
items.description:
Kamta Prasad has been shuttling between government offices in Delhi trying to prove he is not dead.
The 53-year-old tailor is among 130 million names removed from India’s electoral rolls under a voter roll revision that has sparked mass protests and posed the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has led to removals for reasons ranging from “logical discrepancies” to people being recorded as dead, leaving many such as Prasad struggling to get more than just their voting status restored.

items.title: Pakistan, Qatar agree to strengthen internal security cooperation
items.description:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, have agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in internal security, according to a statement issued by the Interior Ministry on Tuesday.
The two met in Doha and held a detailed exchange of views on enhancing cooperation in internal security, the statement said.
They also discussed the current regional situation and matters relating to peace and stability.
“The meeting reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation between the two interior ministries,” the statement said

items.description:

items.title: Senate approves bill seeking blue passports for ex-lawmakers with incomplete term
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday passed a bill that sought to allow former lawmakers to have blue passports even if they had not served a full term in the National Assembly (NA) or Senate.
In the same sitting, a bill seeking to allow the issuance of blue passports to dependent children under the age of 28 of ex-members of Parliament was withdrawn.

items.description:

items.title: Four capital police officials arrested for ‘dacoity’ at Chinese nationals’ house
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Four capital police officials allegedly involved in a dacoity at the house of Chinese nationals in the capital’s F-7/1 sector have been arrested, a police officer confirmed.

The officer said the four officials, who were in uniform, committed the dacoity along with an accomplice. The police arrested all four officials and initiated legal proceedings against them.

items.title: PM warns against resistance to FBR reforms
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday warned tax officers that resistance to the ongoing reforms in the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) would not be tolerated, directing the authorities to implement proposed measures to minimise the country’s tax gap.

The prime minister’s warning came during a weekly briefing on tax reforms, following a call for a pen-down strike by the Inland Revenue Officers Association. items.title: CDF Munir to visit Tehran today
items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir is due to visit Tehran on Tuesday (today), according to a Pakistani official and Iranian media. 

The scheduled visit follows earlier talks between Field Marshal Munir and Iranian leaders in the summer that focused on measures to prevent further escalation and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

Published in Dawn, October 20th, 2026

items.description:
ISLAMABAD: Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly (NA) Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday demanded on the floor of the House that details about Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts be shared.
